summary: Independent review of corrective task 21.7 (fix SEC-21.5-01: the plugin's four named provider HTTP clients must never follow an HTTP redirect, so X-Api-Key cannot be re-sent to a 3xx Location origin). The fix is small, correct, and complete: RegisterProviderHttpClients now configures a primary handler for all four named clients with AllowAutoRedirect=false (the two strict names through the new CreateStrictHandler, both .Insecure names through the existing CreateInsecureHandler, which keeps DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator), and both ClassifyStatus methods gained an explicit >=300 and <400 arm that fails closed as the bounded InvalidResponse/ArrErrorRetryability.Never error with a fixed code-owned literal. I independently reproduced the pre-fix failure by reverting only ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs to its HEAD version and re-running the focused class: Failed 5 / Passed 5 / Total 10, with all four redirect theory cases failing on Assert.Empty() showing the second origin's recorded 'GET /collect' and the registration-shape case failing on an empty handler-action list - exactly the discriminating counter-case criterion 5 requires. I restored the file (sha256 verified) and confirmed the working diff is byte-identical to the pre-review diff. I re-ran the default suite (Failed 0 / Passed 1937 / Skipped 66 / Total 2003), the host-guarded suite against the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host (Failed 0 / Passed 1957 / Skipped 46 / Total 2003), the forced-native pinned-oracle suite that renders the committed goldens (Failed 0 / Passed 2024 / Skipped 21 / Total 2045), the pre-task baseline (filtering out the new class: Failed 0 / Passed 1927 / Skipped 66 / Total 1993, so the delta is exactly the +10 new cases), build (0 warnings / 0 errors), render-docs-state --check (up to date, PLANS.md and state.json agree), and check-docs.sh. The diff is confined to the three source files, the one new test, and the expected documentation surfaces; no golden, RenderVersion, renderer schema, configuration shape, dependency, or agent-prompt change. ADR-005 decision text is untouched (lines 1-166 byte-identical; only an appended 'Implementation note (v1.2, task 21.7)' before References), and docs/decisions/00-index.md is unchanged because no ADR was amended. All eight acceptance criteria are met. The only outstanding item is the contract-defined transient documentation state: state.json does not yet list this reviewer report, which the orchestrator's own Report and Commit Gate adds at commit time.

findings.summary: Switching the two strict clients from the IHttpClientFactory default primary handler to an explicit HttpClientHandler is a neutral transport change; the shared insecure path already used that type.
findings.detail: I confirmed by reflection on the pinned Microsoft.Extensions.Http assembly that the factory default primary handler is SocketsHttpHandler with AllowAutoRedirect=True, and that a plain 'new HttpClientHandler { AllowAutoRedirect = false }' differs from it only in redirect-following among the observable defaults (UseCookies, AutomaticDecompression=None, UseProxy are identical; the factory's handler rotation still bounds the pooled connection lifetime). The insecure clients already used HttpClientHandler before this task, so the two policies remain consistent, and handler pooling and the DI shape are unchanged. No dependency, proxy, cookie, or decompression behaviour is affected.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: (1) Given a provider origin that answers 302 with a Location naming a different origin, the plugin issues no request to that other origin, and the X-Api-Key value is never sent to it.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: ProviderRedirectIsNotFollowedAndTheKeyNeverReachesTheTarget runs for all four named clients over two real loopback origins with the real registrator, ArrHttpClientFactory, and Sonarr/Radarr clients, asserts Assert.Single(provider.Requests) with the key header, then Assert.Empty(target.Requests) after the 302 (tests/ArrTags.Tests/ProviderRedirectTransportTests.cs:77-112). I reproduced the counter-case: with ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs reverted to HEAD, all four theory cases fail at line 97 with 'Assert.Empty() Failure: Collection was not empty / Collection: ["GET /collect HTTP/1.1...", the second origin's recorded request. The assertion is on the second origin's recorder, not on the response outcome, so it genuinely proves non-egress. The origins bind dynamic loopback ports (TcpListener with port 0), so there is no fixed-port collision, and the 250 ms observation window is not a race: the origin enqueues the request before writing the response, so a followed hop is recorded before SendAsync returns.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: (2) All four named provider clients (strict Sonarr, strict Radarr, and both opt-in insecure-TLS clients) are registered with redirect-following disabled; a registration that drops the setting fails a test.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: RegisterProviderHttpClients configures all four names (ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:226-238); rg 'AddHttpClient' src/ shows exactly these four and no other provider transport. AllFourNamedProviderClientsForbidRedirectsAndKeepTheirTlsPolicy resolves the real IOptionsMonitor<HttpClientFactoryOptions> per name, runs the registered builder actions, and asserts FollowsRedirects is false; it fails both when the handler action is dropped (empty action list) and when a handler is registered with redirect-following left on, because FollowsRedirects(null) is defined as true. Reproduced: the pre-fix registration fails this case with 'Assert.NotEmpty() Failure: Collection was empty'.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: (3) The opt-in insecure-TLS relaxation still works and does not re-enable redirect-following or change the header.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The certificate-callback line in CreateInsecureHandler is unchanged by the diff and the test asserts it is present on both .Insecure handlers and absent on both strict handlers, with AllowAutoRedirect=false on all four. ConfiguredProviderOriginReceivesTheApiKeyHeader executes all four clients for real and observes the identical 'X-Api-Key: sec-21-5-01-transport-secret' header with the key absent from the request line, so the header contract is unchanged. See finding 21.7-F2 for the disclosed registration-level bound.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: (4) A not-followed 3xx surfaces as a bounded provider error containing no secret, no response body, no header value, and no Location value, and the configured retry bound is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The >=300 and <400 arm in both ClassifyStatus methods yields ArrProviderErrorCode.InvalidResponse with ArrErrorRetryability.Never and a fixed code-owned literal (no provider-controlled text can reach it; the response body is never read on this path because ClassifyStatus runs before ReadContentAsync and the response is disposed by the using in SendAsync). The test asserts the message is within ArrProviderError.MaxMessageLength (512), mentions the redirect, and contains neither the API key, nor the response-body sentinel, nor the response-header sentinel, nor the target Location URL. Retry semantics are unchanged: SonarrClient.SendAsync returns the status error immediately unless Retryability == Later, so a Never 3xx is terminal - the test observes exactly one key-bearing request with TransientRetryCount=2, while a 503 with TransientRetryCount=1 receives exactly two, proving the transient retry path and its bound are intact. No change to OperationalLimits or any default (git diff touches no configuration file).
